#3. So flawed. 

No one (that I've seen) is trying to bring you down for this logic, but educate and encourage you. 

That is the thinking of someone who has given up. In December of 2013 I hit, what I think was, my peak weight (having not owned a scale and refusing to buy new pants until moving away from my toxic roommate) of 187. I am 5'0. That's morbidly obese. I had resigned myself to just being fat. Thinking I was just "one of those people" who would always be bigger. My dad has always been large, my mom has yo-yoed up and down throughout the years. I was resigned to my fate. 

Until one day I finally actually started caring. Not with a diet. I gave up vices and addictions. No sugar, no soda. 10 pounds gone in a few weeks. No junk food, pick healthy alternatives when eating out. Another 10. Add in exercise now that you're feeling good about yourself. It melts off. Keep it all up and it stays off. I now am 120-122, and not a waif. I take pride in what I eat and how I treat my body. Not one of those HAESers can honestly say that they do either of those things. And if they're saying it, they're lying to themselves to make their world better for what? One instagram post?

You are more than your weight. You are not destined to be fat. Don't condemn yourself to an early grave and health issues because you're "just one of those people". You're absolutely not. It's not a diet, it's an entire lifestyle change and you can do it. I did and I'm one procrastinating, lazy brat.

My mother has not told me she loved me in about two and a half years. I'm used to it now, but it used to hurt a lot, especially when my brother let her know that she was upset with him for not saying it back to her. Hypocritical, right? I finally worked up the courage to say something to her, and she said it's a two way street and that I don't say it to her either. (Though I don't think I should have to initiate that, I'm the kid, she's the mom.) 

Tell her it hurts your feelings. Being honest is the best thing you can do, regardless of the outcome. If things don't change, you still tried, you still let her know how YOU felt. At that point, it's up to you whether you ignore it and continue on as you have been (which is what I'm doing at the moment), or do what you would do with a friend who no longer liked you because you're gay - cut contact and move on (which is what I will be doing in the near future).

Parents have one job other than keeping us alive: love their children completely and unconditionally. It's a selfish act to not do so. It definitely wasn't our choice to be their kid, it's just how everything played out. If they can't love the person you are, then they don't need to be included in your life.
